rule_summary: Manufacture from materials of any heading except that of the product; chapter 4 materials at most 20% of weight; sugar at most 40%; sugar plus chapter 4 at most 50%
who_it_binds: Chay foods classed as food preparations (2106.90) that use imported textured soy protein or soy protein concentrate (also heading 2106)
implication: More than 10% by weight of imported 2106 material (general tolerance) makes the product non-originating, so it pays the UK Global Tariff (8% to 12% on these lines). Fillings based on soy isolate (3504), wheat gluten (1109) or domestic textured soy stay originating
notes: Our reading of the rule; a binding origin ruling would confirm.

rule_summary: Manufacture from materials of any heading except that of the product; materials of headings 1006 and 1101 to 1108 at most 20% of weight; materials of chapters 2, 3 and 16 at most 20%; chapter 4 at most 20%; sugar at most 40%
implication: Non-originating flour above 20% of product weight breaks origin; the tolerance cannot exceed the Annex II caps. Rice-paper and rice-flour wrappers from Vietnamese rice are originating
notes: Share of flour in a given dumpling not measured here.

rule_summary: All materials of chapters 10 and 11 used must be wholly obtained
implication: Flour milled in Vietnam from imported wheat is non-originating, so it counts against the 20% cap in ROO-02

rule_summary: Non-originating materials that fail the rule may be used up to 10% of product weight for chapters 2 and 4 to 24 (other than processed fishery products of chapter 16) or 10% of ex-works price for other products; may not exceed any Annex II percentage cap
implication: Sets the 10% allowance used in ROO-01

rule_summary: A change to 1902 to 1904 from any other chapter
implication: Imported wheat flour (chapter 11) is allowed, so wheat-wrapper dumplings can qualify under CPTPP where they fail UKVFTA
notes: UK-CPTPP tariff rate for Vietnamese 1902.20 not checked.

rule_summary: A change from any other subheading, or regional value content of at least 30% (build-up) or 40% (build-down)
implication: Imported textured soy (2106.10) is allowed, so 2106.90 chay foods can qualify under CPTPP where they fail UKVFTA

rule_summary: A change from any other subheading
implication: Textured protein made from isolate, concentrate of another subheading or defatted flour qualifies

rule_summary: Expected to match ROO-01 to ROO-04 because the UK agreement rolled over the EU agreement's origin protocol (inferred)
who_it_binds: All EU exports claiming the 0% rate
implication: The EU has no CPTPP-style alternative, so the recipe limits in ROO-01 and ROO-02 would bind for EU buyers
notes: EUR-Lex returned an empty page to both fetch tools; not verified.
